headline: Kushner says Russia is ‘comfortable’ with a NATO-style pact.
summary: Jared Kushner, Trump's envoy to the Russia-Ukraine talks, says Russia is open to Ukraine having a mutual defense pact with the US and Europe, like NATO's Article 5. Trump is open to it too. Putin signed a ‘declaration of peace’ with Trump and Xi on Thursday. Hours later, Russian forces bombed bridges in Kyiv and a power substation.
cover_answer: That's the promise being discussed. Nothing is signed.
table_question: If someone breaks a promise the same day, do you sign the next one?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: Russia and Ukraine have been fighting a war for a long time. Now some countries are talking about a promise: if the fighting stops and Russia attacks Ukraine again, they will help protect it, like friends who agree to stick up for each other. The president's helper says Russia is okay with that. It's very far from here, and the grown-ups have it.
5-7.why: A promise between friends is the whole idea. Far away is the comfort.
5-7.why_long: A six-year-old takes one vivid thing for the whole event, so the script gives them the promise between friends and leaves the bridges out. Cantor found distance is comfort at this age, so 'very far from here' does more than an explanation of NATO. Shield on: raise it only if they hear it. Expect 'will Russia come here?' No.

8-12.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
8-12.script: Kushner, Trump's envoy to the talks, says Russia could accept the US and Europe promising to defend Ukraine if it's attacked. The catch: Putin signed a ‘declaration of peace’ Thursday, and hours later Russia bombed bridges in Kyiv. A promise is a whistle. It works only if both sides stop.
8-12.why: A promise, then a broken one. They'll spot the gap first.
8-12.why_long: A twelve-year-old is tracking whether people keep their word, and this story tests it: a peace declaration signed Thursday, bridges bombed hours later. The script puts the two events in order and lets the whistle explain: a rule binds only when both sides obey it. Expect 'then why make the deal?' Semafor doesn't say.

13-17.script: Russia signs a peace declaration, then bombs Kyiv's bridges that night. What is a Russian ‘comfortable’ worth? Kushner says Moscow can accept a NATO-style guarantee for Ukraine. Second: France wants NATO itself to reopen Ukraine's membership. Is a copy of Article 5 worth the real one?
13-17.why: A signature and a bombing. Let them weigh one against the other.
13-17.why_long: A thirteen-year-old can hold a signature and a bombing at once and ask what the signature is worth. The script asks that first, then whether a NATO-style promise outside NATO is the real thing or a copy. Kuhn says argument is practised: let them go before you do. Expect 'would America actually fight?' The article doesn't say.

5-7.a: Bridges and a power station. It doesn't say anyone was hurt.

8-12.a: That's the deal on the table. Nothing is signed yet.

8-12.q: Why did Russia bomb Kyiv after signing for peace?
8-12.a: Semafor doesn't say. It reports the signing, then the bombs.

13-17.q: Why not just let Ukraine join NATO?
13-17.a: France wants NATO to reopen it. Kushner's is a pact outside NATO.

13-17.q: Can you trust Russia's word after the bombing?
13-17.a: The bombs fell hours after the signing. The judgment is yours.
